steps.tx: Autosomal recessive enzymatic blocks in adrenal steroidogenesis impair cortisol synthesis, triggering compensatory pituitary hypersecretion and cortical hyperplasia. Accounting for ninety to ninety-five percent of congenital adrenal hyperplasia, **21-hydroxylase deficiency** stems from mutations in the CYP21A2 gene. Absent 21-hydroxylase blocks the conversion of progesterone to deoxycorticosterone and 17-hydroxyprogesterone to 11-deoxycortisol. The loss of cortisol feedback unleashes massive ACTH release, driving steroid precursors upstream of the block into the intact adrenal androgen pathway. Excess dehydroepiandrosterone and androstenedione are converted peripherally into testosterone, virilizing female fetuses and causing severe salt-wasting in neonates.
steps.say: Autosomal recessive enzymatic blocks in adrenal steroidogenesis impair cortisol synthesis, triggering compensatory pituitary hypersecretion. Accounting for ninety percent of congenital adrenal hyperplasia, 21-hydroxylase deficiency stems from mutations in the CYP21A2 gene. Absent 21-hydroxylase blocks conversion of progesterone and 17-hydroxyprogesterone into aldosterone and cortisol precursors. The loss of cortisol feedback unleashes massive ACTH release, shunting precursors into the androgen pathway. Excess androgens virilize female fetuses and trigger neonatal salt-wasting.

steps.tx: Accumulation of steroid intermediates proximal to the enzymatic block provides the definitive biochemical hallmark of 21-hydroxylase impairment. Measuring elevated serum **17-oh progesterone** confirms the diagnosis, forming the foundation of universal newborn heel-prick screening. In the severe classic salt-wasting form, concurrent aldosterone deficiency manifests at one to three weeks of life as an acute salt-wasting crisis, characterized by vomiting, hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia, metabolic acidosis, and hypovolaemic shock. Affected female 46,XX neonates present at birth with ambiguous genitalia (clitoromegaly and labial fusion), whereas male 46,XY infants appear phenotypically normal at birth.
steps.say: Accumulation of steroid intermediates proximal to the enzymatic block provides the definitive biochemical hallmark of 21-hydroxylase impairment. Measuring elevated serum 17-oh progesterone confirms the diagnosis, forming the foundation of newborn screening. In classic salt-wasting forms, concurrent aldosterone deficiency manifests at two weeks as an acute salt-wasting crisis with hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia, and shock. Affected female neonates present with ambiguous genitalia, whereas male infants appear normal at birth.

steps.tx: A distinct enzymatic block in the adrenal cortex pairs androgen excess with low-renin mineralocorticoid hypertension. Caused by mutations in CYP11B1, **11-beta hydroxylase deficiency** blocks the conversion of 11-deoxycortisol to cortisol and 11-deoxycorticosterone (DOC) to corticosterone. Accumulating 11-deoxycorticosterone possesses potent mineralocorticoid activity, driving avid renal sodium retention, plasma volume expansion, suppressed renin activity, hypokalaemia, and early-onset systemic arterial hypertension. Simultaneously, accumulating androgen precursors virilize female 46,XX external genitalia. Demonstrating high serum DOC and 11-deoxycortisol confirms the disorder, managed by oral glucocorticoid replacement to suppress ACTH-driven mineralocorticoid production.
steps.say: A distinct enzymatic block in the adrenal cortex pairs androgen excess with low-renin mineralocorticoid hypertension. Caused by mutations in CYP11B1, 11-beta hydroxylase deficiency blocks conversion of 11-deoxycortisol to cortisol and deoxycorticosterone to corticosterone. Accumulating deoxycorticosterone possesses mineralocorticoid activity, driving sodium retention, hypokalaemia, and systemic hypertension. Simultaneously, accumulating androgens virilize female genitalia. Oral glucocorticoid replacement suppresses ACTH, normalizing blood pressure.

points: CYP21A2 gene defect; elevated 17-OH progesterone

Treatment: Hydrocortisone PLUS Fludrocortisone

points: CYP11B1 gene defect; elevated 11-deoxycorticosterone
DOC stimulates mineralocorticoid receptors

Treatment: Hydrocortisone alone (suppresses DOC)

steps.tx: The most common sex chromosome aneuploidy in human males causes primary hypogonadism characterized by testicular dysgenesis and seminiferous tubule hyalinization. Affecting one in six hundred live male births, **klinefelter syndrome** typically possesses a 47,XXY karyotype resulting from meiotic non-disjunction. Phenotypic features manifest after puberty with tall, eunuchoid stature (span exceeding height), small, firm, fibrotic testes measuring under four millilitres, sparse body hair, and bilateral gynaecomastia predisposing to male breast cancer. Laboratory evaluation reveals hypergonadotropic male hypogonadism with elevated LH and FSH, low testosterone, and azoospermia.
steps.say: The most common sex chromosome aneuploidy in human males causes primary hypogonadism characterized by testicular dysgenesis. Affecting one in six hundred live male births, klinefelter syndrome possesses a 47,XXY karyotype resulting from meiotic non-disjunction. Phenotypic features manifest after puberty with tall eunuchoid stature, small firm testes, sparse body hair, and bilateral gynaecomastia. Laboratory testing reveals hypergonadotropic male hypogonadism with elevated LH and FSH, low testosterone, and azoospermia.

right.title: Kallmann Syndrome
points: Secondary hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
Failure of GnRH neuron migration; ANOSMIA / hyposmia
Inappropriately low or normal LH and FSH with low testosterone
Delayed puberty, micropenis, cryptorchidism, cleft palate

steps.tx: Defective embryological migration of neuroendocrine neurons from the olfactory placode to the hypothalamus produces congenital secondary hypogonadism paired with olfactory deficits. Termed **kallmann syndrome**, this genetic disorder is caused by mutations in KAL1 (anosmin-1) or FGFR1, disrupting the co-migration of gonadotropin-releasing hormone neurons and olfactory nerve axons. Patients present with delayed puberty, absent secondary sexual development, eunuchoid proportions, micropenis, and cryptorchidism, accompanied by anosmia. Laboratory profiling confirms hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with low testosterone and inappropriately low LH and FSH, responding to testosterone replacement.
steps.say: Defective embryological migration of neuroendocrine neurons from the olfactory placode produces congenital secondary hypogonadism paired with olfactory deficits. Termed kallmann syndrome, this genetic disorder disrupts co-migration of gonadotropin-releasing hormone neurons and olfactory axons. Patients present with delayed puberty, absent sexual development, micropenis, and cryptorchidism, accompanied by anosmia. Laboratory testing confirms hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with low testosterone and low LH, responding to testosterone replacement or gonadotropins.

nodes.label: KAL1 / FGFR1 mutation: Failure of GnRH and olfactory axonal migration
Clinical: Absent pubertal development + complete ANOSMIA (Cannot smell)
Biochemical: Low testosterone + Inappropriately low LH and FSH
Management: Intramuscular / transdermal testosterone OR HCG/FSH for fertility

steps.tx: The commonest endocrine disorder affecting reproductive-aged females combines chronic anovulation with clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenism. Diagnosing **polycystic ovary syndrome** (PCOS) requires fulfilling at least two of the three Rotterdam criteria: ovulatory dysfunction (oligomenorrhoea), hyperandrogenism (manifesting as hirsutism, acne, and alopecia), and polycystic ovarian morphology on pelvic ultrasound showing twelve or more peripheral follicles. PCOS is strongly driven by systemic insulin resistance and compensatory hyperinsulinaemia, which stimulates ovarian theca cell androgen production and inhibits sex hormone-binding globulin.
steps.say: The commonest endocrine disorder affecting reproductive-aged females combines chronic anovulation with clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenism. Diagnosing polycystic ovary syndrome requires fulfilling two of three Rotterdam criteria: ovulatory dysfunction, hyperandrogenism manifesting as hirsutism, and polycystic ovarian morphology on pelvic ultrasound. PCOS is driven by insulin resistance, which stimulates ovarian theca cell androgen production and suppresses sex hormone-binding globulin. Therapy combines lifestyle modification, metformin, and oral contraceptives.

steps.tx: Complete loss-of-function mutations in the intracellular nuclear androgen receptor produce female phenotypic development in genotypic males. Designated as **androgen insensitivity syndrome**, affected individuals possess a normal 46,XY karyotype and functional bilateral intra-abdominal testes secreting normal male levels of testosterone and anti-Mullerian hormone (AMH). Because peripheral target tissues cannot respond to androgens, external genitalia develop along female pathways, producing normal female breast development from peripheral testosterone aromatization. However, because AMH regresses Mullerian structures, patients present with primary amenorrhoea and an absent uterus.
steps.say: Complete loss-of-function mutations in the nuclear androgen receptor produce female phenotypic development in genotypic males. Designated as androgen insensitivity syndrome, affected individuals possess a 46,XY karyotype and functional testes secreting testosterone and anti-Mullerian hormone. Because peripheral tissues cannot respond to androgens, external genitalia develop along female pathways, producing female breast development from aromatization. However, because anti-Mullerian hormone regresses Mullerian ducts, patients present with primary amenorrhoea and absent uterus.

points: 46,XY Genotype with functional intra-abdominal testes

right.title: Mullerian Agenesis (Mayer-Rokitansky)
points: 46,XX Normal female karyotype with normal functioning ovaries
Normal female androgen and estrogen hormone profiles
Congenital absence of uterus and upper two-thirds of vagina
Normal female pubic and axillary hair development

steps.tx: Lifelong endocrine management of congenital adrenal hyperplasia requires balancing adrenal suppression against the iatrogenic risks of Cushing syndrome. Administering oral hydrocortisone suppresses excessive hypothalamic-pituitary ACTH drive, halting adrenal androgen hyperproduction while replacing deficient cortisol. In classic salt-wasting disease, oral fludrocortisone restores mineralocorticoid activity, maintaining normal blood pressure, sodium, and plasma renin activity. Monitoring treatment adequacy requires serial measurements of **steroid profiles**, ensuring 17-hydroxyprogesterone and androstenedione are suppressed without inducing growth retardation, obesity, or secondary hypertension in growing children.

In salt-wasting disease, oral fludrocortisone restores mineralocorticoid activity, maintaining normal blood pressure and electrolytes. Monitoring requires serial measurements of steroid profiles, ensuring androgens are suppressed without impairing growth.
